p: cunning work shalt thou make them: That is, of most cunning or fine work.
in the coupling: On the side that the curtains might be tied together.
second: In tying together both the sides.
covering upon the tabernacle: Lest rain and weather should mar it.
sixth curtain in the forefront of: That is, five on the one side, and five on the other, and the sixth should hang over the door of the tabernacle.
remnant that remaineth of the curtains: For these curtains were two cubits longer than the curtain of the tabernacle so that they were wider by a cubit of both sides.
covering for the tent of rams': To be put on the covering that was made of goats hair.
badgers' skins: This was the third covering of the tabernacle.
coupled together above the head of: The Hebrew word signifies twins declaring that they should be as perfect and well joined as possible.
hooks shall be of gold: Some read "heads of the pillars".
most holy: In which only the high priest entered and only once a year.
without the vail: Meaning, in the holy place.
hanging for the door of the: This hanging or veil was between the holy place, and there where the people were.
